cases.n: Black Axe in Palermo — 14 convicted (2018), 4 acquitted of mafia association (2019)
cases.who: Black Axe (Nigerian confraternity) cell in Palermo
cases.d: A Palermo police operation on 18 November 2016 arrested 19 alleged members of a Black Axe cell based in the Ballarò district; prosecutors said it ran debt collection, exploitation of prostitution and drug trafficking with mafia-style initiation rites. On 21 May 2018 a Palermo judge (fast-track procedure) convicted 14 Nigerians to a combined 87 years. In November 2019 the Palermo Corte d'Assise, trying five others, did not accept the mafia-association charge: four were acquitted and one was jailed for 11 years for kidnapping and sexual violence.
cases.cite: BlogSicilia, 21 May 2018; Il Fatto Quotidiano, 9 Nov 2019

cases.n: IOM: up to 80% of Nigerian women and girls arriving in Italy may be sex-trafficking victims
cases.victims_note: more than 11,000 Nigerian women and girls arrived by boat in 2016 (from 1,500 in 2014), at least four in five forced into prostitution, per IOM data cited by Thomson Reuters Foundation
cases.who: Nigerian trafficking networks via Libya
cases.d: In July 2017 the International Organization for Migration said perhaps 80 per cent of Nigerian migrant women and girls arriving by sea in Italy could be sex-trafficking victims, and that its Italy office had seen an almost 600 per cent rise in potential victims over three years. IOM indicators included age (most victims 13–24) and being 'controlled' by other migrants. Thomson Reuters Foundation later cited IOM data that Nigerian female arrivals rose from 1,500 in 2014 to more than 11,000 in 2016.
cases.cite: UN News (IOM report), 21 Jul 2017; Thomson Reuters Foundation via The Peninsula, 19 Sep 2018

cases.n: Oba of Benin revokes trafficking 'juju' oaths (March 2018)
cases.who: Oba of Benin, Ewuare II; Edo traditional priests
cases.d: In March 2018 the Oba of Benin, Ewuare II, publicly revoked the curses that juju priests had used to bind trafficking victims to their traffickers and laid a curse on anyone involved in trafficking within his domain. Thomson Reuters Foundation reported in September 2018 that anecdotal evidence suggested trafficking had slowed, and cited UNODC that at least nine in ten Nigerian women trafficked to Europe come from Edo State.
cases.cite: New York Times, 24 Mar 2018 (via Wikipedia 'Ewuare II'); Thomson Reuters Foundation via The Peninsula, 19 Sep 2018

cases.n: Nigeria — cult-linked networks traffic women and girls to Europe and West African mines (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Nigerian organized trafficking networks, some linked to cult organizations/confraternities
cases.d: The 2025 US Trafficking in Persons report says highly organized groups, sometimes linked to Nigerian cult organizations or confraternities, recruit and exploit Nigerian women and girls in sex trafficking in Italy, Spain and the UK, and that networks move women and girls to mining regions in Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. In the reporting year courts convicted 49 traffickers and the government identified 2,058 victims. It describes corruption and official complicity, including among officials responsible for anti-trafficking, as significant concerns.
cases.cite: US Department of State, 2025 Trafficking in Persons Report — Nigeria

cases.n: Libya — sex trafficking of sub-Saharan girls in southern brothels; abuse of transiting children (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Commercial sex rings; armed groups; officials
cases.cover: Observers report systemic official complicity, including Libyan Coast Guard, immigration and security officials; the government has never reported prosecuting or convicting anyone for sex or labour trafficking.
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says commercial sex rings subject sub-Saharan women and girls to sex trafficking in brothels, particularly in Ubari, Sabha and Murzuq, and that Nigerian women and girls are at increased risk. It cites an international organization finding that 77 per cent of children and youth transiting Libya experienced indicators of exploitation amounting to trafficking.
cases.cite: US Department of State, 2025 TIP Report — Libya

cases.n: Michael Pepe — former US Marine jailed 210 years for abusing girls in Cambodia
cases.victims_note: eight victims testified at the 2021 retrial; some were 9 years old
cases.who: Michael Joseph Pepe (retired US Marine Corps captain)
cases.d: Pepe travelled to Cambodia in 2005, was arrested there in 2006 and charged in the US in 2007. His first conviction was overturned by the Ninth Circuit in 2018; at a retrial in August 2021 victims testified he drugged, bound, beat and raped them, and prosecutors showed homemade abuse material. On 14 February 2022 a Los Angeles federal judge sentenced him to 210 years. The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and the Cambodian National Police.
cases.cite: US Attorney's Office, Central District of California, 14 Feb 2022

cases.n: Ronald Boyajian — 70 years for buying a 9-year-old girl in Svay Pak
cases.victims_note: four victims aged 8–11 testified; conviction concerned a nine-year-old girl
cases.who: Ronald Gerard Boyajian (US registered sex offender)
cases.d: Boyajian, a registered sex offender with 1995 California convictions, was arrested in Cambodia in February 2009 on what prosecutors called his 35th trip to Asia over nine years, and was among the first three men expelled to the US under ICE's 'Operation Twisted Traveler' in August 2009. Convicted of illicit sexual conduct with a nine-year-old girl in Svay Pak, he was sentenced on 1 August 2016 to 70 years and ordered to pay $40,000 restitution.
cases.cite: US Attorney's Office, CDCA, 1 Aug 2016; AP via NBC News, 31 Aug 2009

cases.n: Operation Twisted Traveler — ICE crackdown on US offenders in Cambodia (2009)
cases.who: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement; Cambodian police
cases.d: In August 2009 three previously convicted US sex offenders arrested by Cambodian police in February — Ronald Boyajian, Erik Peeters and Jack Sporich — were returned to Los Angeles as the first defendants charged under 'Operation Twisted Traveler'. ICE head John Morton called Cambodia 'ground zero for child sex tourism'; ICE had stationed an agent in Cambodia full-time. Peeters was accused of abusing at least three Cambodian boys and Sporich of abusing a boy in Siem Reap (accusations at the time).
cases.cite: Associated Press via NBC News, 31 Aug 2009

cases.n: Svay Pak child brothels — 2003 raid and later decline
cases.cover: The 22 January 2003 police raid was widely advertised in advance; almost all children had been moved and no pimps or clients were arrested. Local authorities had extorted brothel owners.
cases.who: Brothels in Svay Pak (mostly ethnic Vietnamese victims)
cases.d: Brothels in Svay Pak, a village north of Phnom Penh, proliferated in the 1990s; in May 2000 there were 24 brothels with about 320 women on two streets, and in 2002 children, mostly ethnic Vietnamese sold by poor families, were exploited by Western child-sex tourists. A police raid in January 2003 after ministerial and ASEAN pressure was announced in advance. ABC News in 2017 found the share of children among those in sex work had fallen to 1–2% from 35%.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Svay Pak' (citing Haugen 2005, Daily Telegraph, Dateline NBC, ABC News 2017)

cases.n: Cambodia — child sex tourism and brothels; scam compounds (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: The report says official complicity, including at senior levels, inhibited effective law enforcement.
cases.who: Brothel and entertainment operators; foreign and Cambodian offenders
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says Cambodian men and men from Australia, South Africa, the United States and other countries in Asia and Europe sexually exploit children in the tourism industry, increasingly via social media; children as young as 13 are exploited in brothels to pay family debts; and women and girls are exploited in online scam compounds.
cases.cite: US Department of State, 2025 TIP Report — Cambodia

cases.n: Lake Volta, Ghana — child trafficking in fishing (IJM prevalence study 2023)
cases.who: Fishing-boat owners and intermediaries on Lake Volta
cases.d: A 2023 International Justice Mission household survey of 1,286 children in three fishing districts around Lake Volta estimated that about 37.7 per cent were likely trafficked and a further 45.1 per cent were in likely exploitative child labour. The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit children as young as four in Lake Volta's fishing industry, controlling them with violence and limited food, and that girls in the fishing sector are vulnerable to sexual exploitation; it notes observers reported forced child labour on the lake has decreased.
cases.cite: International Justice Mission, 2023 Fishing Prevalence Study Report; US TIP Report 2025 — Ghana

cases.n: Senegal — forced begging and abuse of talibé children in Quranic schools (HRW 2019)
cases.victims_note: HRW estimates over 100,000 talibé children are forced to beg; 2017–2018 documentation: 16 deaths, 61 beatings, 15 cases of actual or attempted rape or sexual abuse
cases.who: Some marabouts (Quranic teachers) running residential daaras
cases.d: Human Rights Watch and the Senegalese PPDH platform reported on 11 June 2019 that over 100,000 talibé children in Senegal are forced by some Quranic teachers to beg daily, often under quotas enforced by beatings. For 2017–2018 they documented 16 deaths of talibés from beatings, neglect or endangerment, 61 cases of beatings, 15 cases of actual or attempted rape or sexual abuse and 14 cases of children chained or imprisoned, in 8 of Senegal's 14 regions. The 2025 US TIP report says the government identified 573 child forced-begging victims in the year.
cases.cite: Human Rights Watch & PPDH, 'There Is Enormous Suffering', 11 Jun 2019; US TIP Report 2025 — Senegal

cases.n: Kédougou, Senegal — sex trafficking of girls at gold-mining sites
cases.who: Trafficking networks supplying mining camps
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit women and girls as young as 12 in sex trafficking throughout Senegal's southeastern gold-mining region of Kédougou; most victims are from Nigeria, with others from Senegal, Mali, Benin, Burkina Faso, Ghana, Guinea, Sierra Leone and China. It also reports some tourists exploit children in Dakar and Saint-Louis, and to a lesser extent Cap Skirring and La Petite Côte.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Senegal

cases.n: Kenya coast — UNICEF/Government study on child sex tourism (2006)
cases.victims_note: 2,000–3,000 girls and boys in full-time commercial sex in the coastal resorts; up to 30% of 12–18-year-old girls in the areas involved in casual sex work
cases.who: Tourists and local clients in Kenya's beach resorts
cases.d: On 19 December 2006 UNICEF and Kenya's Ministry of Home Affairs launched a joint study of four beach resort areas. It found that up to 30 per cent of 12–18-year-old girls living there were involved in casual sex work and that two to three thousand children were in full-time commercial sex; 38 per cent of clients were Kenyan and 44 per cent Italian, German or Swiss tourists. Vice President Moody Awori accepted the findings and acknowledged police and community failure to enforce the law.
cases.cite: UNICEF & Government of Kenya, 'The Extent and Effect of Sex Tourism and Sexual Exploitation of Children on the Kenyan Coast' (2006), as summarised in US Embassy Nairobi cable 06NAIROBI5304, 20 Dec 2006

cases.n: Kenya — child sex trafficking in Kilifi/Kwale villas; Karamoja girls to Nairobi (US TIP 2025)
cases.victims_note: NGO 2023 estimate of more than 2,000 children exploited in Kilifi and Kwale
cases.cover: The report notes ongoing concerns of official complicity with no reported action against complicit officials.
cases.who: Family members, taxi drivers, recruiters; foreign and local offenders
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report cites a 2023 NGO study estimating that more than 2,000 children were exploited in child sex trafficking in Kilifi and Kwale counties, increasingly in private villas and vacation homes rather than hotels. It also reports cross-border rings moving women and underage girls from Uganda's Karamoja region to Nairobi, and truck drivers, miners and Lake Victoria fishermen exploiting children.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Kenya

cases.n: The Gambia — child sex tourism on the Senegambia Strip (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Organized networks using European and Gambian travel agencies
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says European tourists, primarily from the UK, reportedly travel to The Gambia to exploit children, and that organized sex-trafficking networks use European and Gambian travel agencies to promote the country as a destination, especially the Senegambia Strip. Women and girls from other West African countries, especially Nigeria, are recruited for tourism jobs and then sexually exploited. The Tourism Offences Act provides life imprisonment for child trafficking by tourists.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — The Gambia; Wikipedia 'Prostitution in the Gambia'

cases.n: Madagascar — child sex tourism and karaoke-bar exploitation (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: The report calls corruption and official complicity significant concerns; one official was investigated.
cases.who: Malagasy and foreign offenders
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says most child sex-trafficking victims are exploited by Malagasy men, but foreign tourists, often from France, also exploit children; parents sometimes encourage daughters into commercial sex with tourists, and children are exploited in Antananarivo karaoke bars. Courts convicted 15 traffickers, the first convictions in four years. A Nosy Be anti-trafficking committee exists. In July 2025 police in Nosy Be arrested two women suspected of filming abuse of their own children and selling the videos to foreign buyers via mobile money (charged; L'Express de Madagascar).
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Madagascar; L'Express de Madagascar, Jul 2025

cases.n: Morocco — royal pardon of Spanish child rapist Daniel Galván (2013)
cases.victims_note: at least eleven Moroccan children
cases.cover: King Mohammed VI pardoned Galván on 30 July 2013 among 48 Spanish prisoners; he left Morocco on an expired passport with authorities' knowledge before the pardon was cancelled. Protesters in Rabat were violently dispersed. A 2010 US cable reported a 2006 royal pardon of a French man convicted of abusing a 15-year-old boy in Marrakesh.
cases.who: Daniel Galván Viña
cases.d: Galván, a Spanish national living in Kenitra, was arrested in 2011 and sentenced to 30 years for raping at least eleven Moroccan children. On 30 July 2013 the king pardoned him as part of a gesture to Spain; after public outrage and protests, the pardon was cancelled on 4 August, the first such cancellation. Galván was arrested in Spain on 7 August on a Moroccan warrant; Spanish courts refused extradition.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Daniel Galván scandal' (citing Lakome, El País, MAP); CNN, 4–6 Aug 2013

cases.n: Morocco — foreign offenders in Tangier vacation rentals (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Foreign nationals, primarily from Europe and the Middle East
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says some foreign nationals, primarily from Europe and the Middle East, sexually exploit children in major Moroccan cities, and NGOs report tourists exploit children in Tangier in vacation rentals owned and managed by European nationals. It also reports alleged exploitation of children after the September 2023 Al Haouz earthquake. Courts convicted 60 traffickers in 2024.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Morocco

cases.n: Tanzania — child sex trafficking in Zanzibar and cities (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: The report says the government did not adequately address corruption and official complicity.
cases.who: Traffickers, brokers, foster families
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit children in sex trafficking, including by foreign offenders ('extraterritorial sexual exploitation'), and in forced labour and domestic servitude in Zanzibar, and that women and girls from the mainland are brought to Zanzibar with false promises. Child sex trafficking also occurs in Arusha, Dar es Salaam, Dodoma, Mbeya and Mwanza.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Tanzania

cases.n: Uganda — Karamojong children sold at border markets (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Traffickers including community 'elders'
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says NGOs estimate the majority of child sex-trafficking victims in Uganda are ethnically Karamojong, especially from Napak district. Traffickers, sometimes community 'elders', force children to meet them at international borders, where markets are organized to sell children into domestic servitude or sex trafficking. Women, girls and boys are exploited in Kampala brothels, bars and homes.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Uganda; Kenya

cases.n: Malawi — Dzaleka refugee camp girls recruited for sex trafficking (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: The report says official complicity continued to impede enforcement.
cases.who: Transnational crime syndicates operating from bars and compounds in the camp
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says organized transnational syndicates operating from informal bars and housing in Dzaleka camp (about 53,000 refugees in a space for 10,000) recruit girls for sex trafficking inside the camp and in roadside bars along the highway to Lilongwe; the camp is a waypoint on the 'Southern Route' to South Africa. Girls are also exploited in bars and illegal brothels in Lilongwe and Blantyre.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Malawi

cases.n: Mozambique — girls exploited along the Maputo–South Africa highway and at mines (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Traffickers at rest stops, bars, mining areas; non-state armed groups
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit girls in rest stops, bars and restaurants along the Maputo–South Africa highway and around mines, and that non-state armed groups abducted children and sexually exploited girls. Girls as young as 11 working as nannies are vulnerable when employment ends.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Mozambique

cases.n: Zimbabwe — sex trafficking around gold and diamond mines; girls traded under ngozi (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Traffickers at mining sites; families
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit women and children in sex trafficking around mines, sometimes for money or food, and may exploit children as panners and ore couriers in gold and diamond mines. Traditional practices including trading daughters for food or money and ngozi — giving a relative to another family to atone for a killing — make girls vulnerable. Low-level official complicity persisted.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Zimbabwe

cases.n: DR Congo — forced labour and sexual exploitation of children at eastern artisanal mines (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Traffickers named in the report include government officials; corruption and complicity contributed to impunity.
cases.who: Mining bosses, miners, family members, government officials, armed groups
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says mining bosses, other miners, family members, government officials and armed groups force or coerce adults and children into forced labour in artisanal mines in eastern DRC, including through debt bondage, and that most trafficking is internal, including sex trafficking and forced marriage of girls.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Democratic Republic of the Congo

cases.n: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana — 1.56 million children in cocoa child labour (NORC 2020)
cases.victims_note: estimate for 2018–19; about 1.48 million (95%) in hazardous child labour
cases.who: Cocoa supply chain (farms supplying international chocolate companies)
cases.d: A US Department of Labor-funded study by NORC at the University of Chicago, released 19 October 2020, estimated 1.56 million children were in cocoa-related child labour in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana in 2018–19, 95 per cent in hazardous work, and found child labour had increased since 2008–09 while production rose. Industry had committed in the 2001 Harkin-Engel Protocol and a 2010 declaration to cut the worst forms by 70 per cent by 2020. The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Ghanaian and other West African children in forced labour in cocoa.
cases.cite: NORC, 'Assessing Progress in Reducing Child Labor in Cocoa Production…' (2020), via ConfectioneryNews 19 Oct 2020; US TIP 2025 — Ghana

cases.n: Côte d'Ivoire — girls brought to Abidjan for domestic servitude; Nigerian girls at mines (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Relatives and Nigerian trafficking networks
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says distant relatives bring girls from rural Côte d'Ivoire and other West African countries to Abidjan for school or training and then exploit them in domestic servitude, where they are vulnerable to sexual exploitation; Ivorian women and girls are sex-trafficked especially in Abidjan; and Nigerian traffickers recruit women and girls for shop jobs then exploit them in gold-mining and cocoa regions.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Côte d'Ivoire

cases.n: South Africa — rural children trafficked to Gauteng and Western Cape (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Low-level official corruption and complicity persisted.
cases.who: Brothel owners and traffickers; some parents
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers recruit victims from rural areas, especially children, and exploit them in sex trafficking in cities, especially Gauteng and Western Cape; brothel owners use drugs to control victims including children; and some parents exploit their children in sex trafficking or online sexual exploitation for money or drugs.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — South Africa

cases.n: Ethiopia — girls trafficked to Djibouti, Sudan and Saudi Arabia (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Traffickers and begging rings
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Ethiopian women and children in forced begging, sometimes via organized begging rings, in Saudi Arabia, and exploit Ethiopian girls in domestic servitude and sex trafficking in neighbouring countries, particularly Djibouti and Sudan, sometimes using drugs for control. Reports of official complicity continued.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Ethiopia

cases.n: Nepal → India — trafficking of girls to Indian brothels (estimates)
cases.victims_note: Published annual estimates range from 5,000–10,000 women and girls (Koirala et al.; Poudel & Carryer 2000) and 7,000–10,000 girls aged 9–16 (Aengst 2001); UNDP 2004 said about 20% of those trafficked are under 16
cases.cover: US TIP 2025: serious concerns of official complicity; traffickers bribe some Indian officials to fly Nepali workers to third countries.
cases.who: Trafficking networks recruiting via false job, marriage and online romance offers
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers use job offers and online romance scams to recruit Nepali women and children to India for sex trafficking; Nepali courts convicted 406 traffickers (231 for sex trafficking) in the year. A 2024 study it cites found a majority of workers in Nepal's adult entertainment sector were sex-trafficking victims, nearly half of them children. Research collated on Wikipedia gives estimates of 5,000–10,000 Nepali women and girls trafficked to India each year across a 1,850 km open border.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Nepal; Wikipedia 'Human trafficking in Nepal' (citing Koirala et al., Aengst 2001, UNDP 2004, ILO 2001)

cases.n: Kolkata red-light areas — rescues of trafficked Nepali girls and minors (2015, 2025)
cases.victims_note: six Nepali girls (Jan 2015, IJM-assisted raid) plus nine minor girls rescued in Burtolla (Sept 2025)
cases.who: Brothel keepers and traffickers in Kolkata
cases.d: In January 2015 police, with International Justice Mission and three NGOs, freed six young women trafficked from Nepal from four brothels in Kolkata's largest red-light area; all had fake adult ID documents, which IJM said traffickers issue to underage girls. On 10 September 2025 Kolkata Police's Anti-Human Trafficking Unit rescued ten people including nine minor girls from a house in Burtolla, North Kolkata, and arrested six people, including the couple running it (charged). The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers recruit significant numbers of Nepali and Bangladeshi women and girls for sex trafficking in India.
cases.cite: IJM Canada, 22 Jan 2015; IANS via Free Press Journal, 11 Sep 2025; US TIP 2025 — India

cases.n: Kamathipura, Mumbai — red-light district fed by trafficking from Nepal and Indian states
cases.who: Brothels of Kamathipura
cases.d: Kamathipura in Mumbai grew into what has been called Asia's largest sex district; in recent decades large numbers of Nepalese women and girls were trafficked there, alongside women trafficked from other Indian states. The 2025 US TIP report says buyer concerns about brothels have pushed sex trafficking in India towards spas, hotels and private residences arranged by technology, and that India reported 204 convicted traffickers and 1,134 acquittals in its 2022 crime data.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Kamathipura'; US TIP Report 2025 — India

cases.n: Bangladesh — girls trafficked to India, Pakistan and the Gulf; Rohingya girls near Cox's Bazar (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Corruption and official complicity were significant concerns; corrupt policing in Rohingya camps.
cases.who: Traffickers, recruitment agents, armed groups in Rohingya camps
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Bangladeshi women and girls in sex trafficking abroad, including in India, Pakistan and Gulf countries, and observers estimate children are 40 per cent of Bangladeshi sex-trafficking victims exploited abroad. Tourists have increased demand for sexual exploitation, including of Rohingya girls, near Cox's Bazar, where more than one million Rohingya refugees live in 33 camps. Courts convicted 103 traffickers, down from 407.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Bangladesh

cases.n: Pakistan → China — 629 girls and women sold as 'brides' (AP 2019)
cases.victims_note: girls and women on a list compiled by Pakistani investigators, from 2018 to June 2019
cases.cover: Officials told AP the investigation largely stopped after June 2019 because of pressure from government officials fearful of harming ties with Beijing; in October 2019 a Faisalabad court acquitted 31 Chinese nationals after witnesses were threatened or bribed into silence.
cases.who: Brokers selling poor (often Christian) Pakistani girls and women to Chinese men
cases.d: AP obtained a list compiled by Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency of 629 girls and women sold as brides to Chinese men from 2018 to mid-2019. In October 2019 a court in Faisalabad acquitted 31 Chinese nationals charged in the biggest case. The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers target impoverished Christian communities to send women and girls to China, where hundreds reported being forced into commercial sex.
cases.cite: Associated Press via Al Jazeera, 5 Dec 2019; US TIP 2025 — Pakistan

cases.n: Myanmar → China — Kachin women and girls sold as 'brides' (HRW 2019)
cases.victims_note: Myanmar government reported 226 cases in 2017; HRW interviewed 37 survivors and said the true number is likely much higher
cases.cover: HRW said Myanmar and Chinese authorities were 'looking away'; police on both sides gave traffickers little reason to fear enforcement.
cases.who: Traffickers including relatives and acquaintances; buying families in China
cases.d: Human Rights Watch's 112-page report of 21 March 2019 documented women and girls from Kachin and northern Shan States, many displaced by conflict, sold for US$3,000–13,000 to Chinese families, locked up and raped so they would become pregnant. One survivor was trafficked at 16 by her sister-in-law. The 2025 US TIP report says displaced women and girls in Kachin and Shan remain vulnerable to forced marriage and forced childbearing in China.
cases.cite: Human Rights Watch, 'Give Us a Baby and We'll Let You Go', 21 Mar 2019; US TIP 2025 — Burma

cases.n: Vietnam and Laos → China — girls sold as brides (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Traffickers and marriage brokers
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP reports say traffickers in Vietnamese border villages lure women and girls, particularly Hmong, to China for forced marriages involving sex trafficking or forced labour, and use 'bride kidnapping' to exploit ethnic-minority girls in the northwest highlands; in Laos, traffickers increasingly kidnap or recruit women and girls via marriage brokers to China for sex trafficking, forced labour and forced surrogacy. Vietnam identified 236 child victims in 2024.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Vietnam; Laos

cases.n: Swiss bar owner jailed 16 years for abusing more than 80 boys in Pattaya and northern Thailand
cases.victims_note: more than 80 boys, some as young as nine or ten
cases.who: Unnamed Swiss national (72, from Lucerne) who ran a bar in Pattaya
cases.d: A Swiss man previously convicted of abusing children in Fribourg (1980) and Valais (1991) returned to Thailand in 1996 and, mainly in 2002–2013, abused more than 80 boys in Pattaya, where he ran a bar with a hotel room frequented by Europeans, and in Nong Hoi in the north; he also forced boys to perform acts with European clients. Charged in Fribourg with human trafficking, encouraging prostitution, sexual acts with children and abuse material, he was sentenced by a Swiss court on 1 March 2018 to 16 years.
cases.cite: Al Jazeera, 10 Mar 2017; swissinfo.ch, 1 Mar 2018

cases.n: Mark Frost — 13 life terms for abuse of boys in Thailand and the UK (2017)
cases.victims_note: at least nine children in Thailand; 45 offences in total
cases.who: Mark Frost (also known as Andrew Tracey), former teacher and scout leader
cases.d: Frost, who had held positions of trust in UK schools and scouting and first admitted an offence in 1992, abused boys from poor families in Thailand in 2011–2013, including streaming abuse by webcam to another European man. In February 2017 he was sentenced to 13 terms of life imprisonment after pleading guilty to 45 offences against boys in the UK and Thailand. The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse cited the case as one of only about eight successful UK prosecutions since 1997 for offences committed abroad. Eight Thai boys secured civil compensation in 2018.
cases.cite: Leigh Day, 20 Nov 2018; IICSA 'Protection of Children Outside the UK' report, Jan 2020; Al Jazeera, 10 Mar 2017

cases.n: Patong, Phuket — foreign bar owner sentenced to 1,073 years after raid freed six minors (2024)
cases.cover: Five senior Patong police officers were transferred after the raid; the foreign owner initially fled to a neighbouring country.
cases.who: Illegal bar on Bangla Road
cases.d: A 2023 raid on an illegal bar on Bangla Road, Patong, rescued six victims of child sexual exploitation under 18. On 19 July 2024 the Phuket Provincial Court sentenced seven defendants, Thai and foreign; the prime defendant, a foreign owner, received a total of 1,073 years. Five senior Patong police were transferred after the raid. The 2025 US TIP report says children from Thailand, Burma, Cambodia and Laos are increasingly sex-trafficked in brothels, bars, karaoke lounges and hotels.
cases.cite: The Phuket Express, 19 Jul 2024; US TIP 2025 — Thailand

cases.n: David Timothy Deakin — life sentence, Angeles City court (2020)
cases.victims_note: two girls rescued at arrest
cases.who: David Timothy Deakin (US national)
cases.d: Acting on an FBI referral, the Philippine National Bureau of Investigation arrested US national David Timothy Deakin in Mabalacat, Pampanga, in 2017, rescuing two girls and seizing hard drives of abuse material; IJM said he abused Filipino children, recorded it and sold it online to foreign customers. In May 2020 the Angeles City Regional Trial Court Branch 58 convicted him of large-scale human trafficking and sentenced him to life imprisonment, in the country's first conviction delivered by videoconference. The 2025 US TIP report names Angeles City among tourist destinations with high demand for commercial sex.
cases.cite: Philstar, 28 May 2020; US TIP 2025 — Philippines

cases.n: Philippines — foreign offenders and child sex trafficking in tourist towns (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Corruption and official complicity remained significant concerns.
cases.who: Foreign offenders; family members; brothel and bar operators
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says sex trafficking frequently occurs in tourist destinations such as Boracay, Angeles City, Olongapo, Puerto Galera and Surigao. Many foreign offenders are convicted or charged sex offenders at home, most commonly from Australia, Japan, New Zealand, the UK and the US, with more reports from Canada, Morocco, Iraq and Denmark. Courts convicted 143 traffickers, 120 for sex trafficking.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Philippines

cases.n: Indonesia — child sexual exploitation in the Riau Islands and 'contract marriages' in Puncak (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: The report says the government tacitly accepted 'contract marriages'; corruption and complicity significantly impeded efforts.
cases.who: Foreign offenders; brokers of 'contract marriages'
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says extraterritorial child sexual exploitation is prevalent in the Riau Islands bordering Singapore, and women and girls are coerced into commercial sex notably in Batam. It also reports that Middle Eastern tourists pay more than $700 for week-long 'contract marriages' in Puncak, Bogor, involving girls as young as nine, a practice the government tacitly accepted. In October 2017 Batam police arrested a Singaporean man accused of molesting three boys (IBTimes, charged).
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Indonesia; IBTimes UK, Oct 2017

cases.n: Japan — 'JK business' and compensated dating (police survey 2024; US TIP 2025)
cases.who: JK businesses, often with organized-crime ties
cases.d: The 'JK business' sells simulated dates and services with high-school girls. A National Police Agency survey at the end of December 2024 counted 91 establishments advertising in this way, 70 per cent in Tokyo. Kanagawa first regulated it in 2011 and Tokyo enacted a dedicated ordinance in 2017. The 2025 US TIP report says JK variants and 'compensated dating', often tied to organized crime, continue to facilitate sex trafficking of Japanese children and of children from China, South Korea, Laos, the Philippines, Singapore and Vietnam.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'JK business' (citing National Police Agency); US TIP 2025 — Japan

cases.n: South Korea — runaway children in commercial sex; police officer convicted (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: NGOs previously reported some local police sexually exploited children; one officer was convicted (bribery, secrecy violations) and another acquitted.
cases.who: Entertainment establishments, escort services, chat-room operators
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit South Korean women and children, including runaways, in bars, nightclubs and internet-advertised escort services, and chat-room operators coerce children with compromising images into producing sexual material. A court convicted a local police officer in a 2022 case involving alleged complicity in trafficking-related crimes and sentenced him to five years; another officer was acquitted.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — South Korea

cases.n: Mongolia — girls sex-trafficked in Ulaanbaatar hotels and karaoke bars (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: The report says exploitation is sometimes facilitated by lack of police enforcement; some families are complicit.
cases.who: Traffickers in hotels, massage parlours, karaoke clubs
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says women and girls are sex-trafficked in Mongolian hotels, massage parlours, illegal brothels, bars and karaoke clubs, mostly in Ulaanbaatar, provincial centres and border areas, sometimes facilitated by a lack of police enforcement; traffickers use online platforms to groom and blackmail children; and children taken abroad for competitions have instead been put to work, e.g. as horse jockeys.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Mongolia

cases.n: Sri Lanka — child sex tourism in coastal areas (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Foreign and local offenders
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers reportedly exploit boys and girls in child sex trafficking, including in coastal areas, for foreign offenders, and recommends investigating complicit establishments. The government convicted six traffickers and identified seven child victims in the year.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Sri Lanka

cases.n: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan — girls lured to cities; children in institutions (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Traffickers recruiting via social media
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers lure girls and women from rural Kazakhstan and neighbouring Central Asian, East Asian and Eastern European countries with job offers as waitresses, models or nannies in large cities, and exploit Kazakh women and girls in Russia, Uzbekistan, the Middle East, Europe, East Asia and the US. In Uzbekistan, children in institutions are vulnerable to sex trafficking.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Kazakhstan; Uzbekistan

cases.n: Medellín — US federal prosecutions of travelling offenders (10 convictions by May 2026)
cases.victims_note: Count of US sentences reported by Medellín mayor's office and BluRadio; individual cases cover at least five victims (Poceiro) and a 14-year-old (Arellano Sandoval)
cases.who: US-national travelling offenders; HSI Colombia; Alcaldía de Medellín
cases.d: BluRadio reported on 21 May 2026 that US courts, working with Colombian authorities and the Medellín mayor's office, had handed down a tenth sentence in an offensive against foreigners exploiting children in Medellín: Ramón Arellano Sandoval, 65, sentenced in Miami to 30 years for attempted sexual exploitation of a 14-year-old Medellín girl, who had entered the city 48 times in two years. On 22 January 2026 Manuel Poceiro, 69, of Miami, was sentenced to life for travelling to Colombia to exploit minors, after HSI found material involving at least five minors. In March 2024 US national Timothy Alan Livingston was found in a Medellín hotel with two minors (aged between 12 and 16, per police sources); a Colombian judge issued an arrest warrant and Interpol a blue notice (charged, at large at the time).
cases.cite: BluRadio, 21 May 2026; US Attorney's Office SDFL, 22 Jan 2026; El Tiempo, 9 Apr 2024; La FM, Apr 2024

cases.n: Cartagena — 'La Madame' network exploiting girls for tourists (plea 2018)
cases.cover: At hearings she threatened to reveal the names of politicians and powerful men she said were clients (her claim, unverified).
cases.who: Liliana del Carmen Campos Puello ('La Madame')
cases.d: Liliana del Carmen Campos Puello ran a sex network from a Bocagrande apartment in Cartagena, supplying young women and minors to parties on yachts, in hotels and at beaches and sending women to Panama, Mexico, Miami and the Bahamas; prosecutors seized 15 ledgers of clients and payments, and a WhatsApp group listed 200 women. In 2018 she accepted charges of human trafficking and conspiracy in a plea deal and was sentenced to eight years and one month; she was released on parole in 2023. US ICE supported the investigation.
cases.cite: La FM, 2018; El Comercio (Peru), 6 Aug 2018; Noticias RCN, 2023

cases.n: Colombia — Tren de Aragua sex trafficking of Venezuelan girls; webcam industry (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Two complicit officials received plea-deal sentences of 7.5 years, below the statutory minimum.
cases.who: Tren de Aragua; ELN; webcam studios
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says Tren de Aragua and the ELN run sex-trafficking networks in Villa del Rosario, Norte de Santander, and Tren de Aragua uses Cúcuta's transport hub to move victims to Argentina, Ecuador and Peru and operates in Bogotá, Cali, Medellín and Pereira. Traffickers recruit women and girls, mostly Colombians and displaced Venezuelans, into 'webcam modelling', an industry likely worth over $1.2 billion a year. Sex trafficking of girls is prevalent in tourist areas and extractive zones.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Colombia

cases.n: Sosúa — 29 trafficking victims including 20 minors freed in US–Dominican sting (2015)
cases.victims_note: including 20 minors aged 14–17
cases.who: Local pimping ring in a tourist town
cases.d: In April 2015 Dominican authorities, with HSI Santo Domingo and two private US organisations, lured alleged traffickers to a staged 'sex party' in the tourist town of Sosúa, freeing 29 victims including 20 minors aged 14–17 and arresting seven Dominican nationals (two women, five men), who faced up to 15 years. The 2025 US TIP report says teenage girls are frequently exploited on streets, in parks and on beaches, and NGOs link rising child victim numbers to weak regulation of tourism.
cases.cite: Latin Times, Apr 2015 (citing El Periódico, US Embassy); US TIP 2025 — Dominican Republic

cases.n: Troy Brimm — 34 years for travelling to Puerto Plata to abuse boys (2013)
cases.who: Troy Douglas Brimm, of Modesto, California
cases.d: Brimm, 50, was convicted on two counts of travelling to Puerto Plata, Dominican Republic, to engage in illicit sexual conduct with minor boys, including shoe-shine boys, after a flight on 20 October 2009. On 10 January 2013 a Miami federal judge sentenced him to 34 years followed by lifetime supervised release. The case was investigated by HSI Miami with the Dominican National Police and the Puerto Plata Prosecutor's Office.
cases.cite: US Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida, 11 Jan 2013

cases.n: La Pampa, Madre de Dios — Operación Mercurio 2019 and sex trafficking in mining camps
cases.victims_note: number of minors rescued in Mercurio 2019 not stated in sources opened
cases.who: Bar/brothel networks serving illegal gold-mining camps
cases.d: On 19–20 February 2019 more than 1,500 military and police began Operación Mercurio against illegal gold mining in La Pampa, in the Tambopata reserve buffer zone, under a state of emergency. Peru's Women's Minister said the worst crimes, including child sexual exploitation and child labour, had been committed there, and her ministry took in minors and women rescued from trafficking. Reporting in 2022 said police were still dismantling networks recruiting women to La Pampa bars; a 16-year-old girl previously rescued from a La Pampa trafficking band was found murdered at km 108 in April 2021.
cases.cite: Andina, 20 Feb 2019; Diálogo Américas, 2019; Actualidad Ambiental, 15 Feb 2022; US TIP 2025 — Peru

cases.n: Peru — foreign tourists exploit children in Cusco, Lima and the Amazon (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Authorities charged two police officers for crimes against trafficking victims; corruption remained a significant concern.
cases.who: Criminal groups transporting tourists on the Amazon
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says tourists from the US and Europe exploit children in Cusco, Lima and the Peruvian Amazon, and in Loreto criminal groups take foreign tourists by boat to remote venues on the Amazon River where women and children are exploited. Peruvian, Venezuelan and Bolivian women and girls are lured to mining and logging camps. Courts convicted 59 traffickers in 2024.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Peru

cases.n: Brazil — Federal Highway Police 'Projeto Mapear' of child sexual exploitation points on highways
cases.victims_note: Mapear 2021–22: 9,700+ points surveyed, 640 critical; 2023 operations rescued 138 minors, 14 being sexually exploited
cases.who: Truck stops, bars, motels along federal highways
cases.d: Brazil's Federal Highway Police (PRF) and Childhood Brasil have mapped roadside sites vulnerable to child sexual exploitation for about 19 years. The 2021–2022 survey, released 31 May 2023, assessed more than 9,700 points, rating 640 critical and about 1,800 high-risk; the worst conditions were on BR-116 (12 critical points), BR-153, BR-101, BR-163, BR-232 and BR-040. An earlier edition found 69% of victims female and 22% transgender, and 38% from elsewhere, possibly trafficked. The 2025 US TIP report says child sex trafficking is common along BR-386, BR-116 and BR-255.
cases.cite: SBT News, 1 Jun 2023; Brasil 61 (PRF/Childhood Brasil); US TIP 2025 — Brazil

cases.n: Brazil — child sex tourism in northeastern coastal cities (Fortaleza, Natal, Recife, Salvador)
cases.cover: US TIP 2025: no investigations of complicit officials reported; a 2016 child sex-trafficking case involving an elected official in Paraná unresolved.
cases.who: Taxi drivers, hotel and bar staff facilitating foreign offenders
cases.d: In 2006 Brazil's Federal Police described sex tourism as most frequent in Fortaleza, Recife, Salvador and Natal, and ran periodic raids, e.g. on a Ponta Negra (Natal) nightclub with 110 foreigners (no children found that night). The 2025 US TIP report says taxi drivers and hotel, bar and nightclub staff in coastal tourist destinations facilitate child sex trafficking, and cites a study suggesting up to 16 per cent of girls aged 14–17 in one northeastern metropolitan area were likely victims of commercial sexual exploitation.
cases.cite: Agência Brasil, 4 Apr 2006; US TIP 2025 — Brazil

cases.n: Bolivia — foreign offenders in Indigenous communities near Rurrenabaque (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Foreign offenders; parents; online abuse-material producers
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says foreign offenders exploited children in rural Indigenous communities in northern La Paz department, in and around Rurrenabaque and Santa Cruz, and in tourist areas of La Paz and Beni; production of abuse material for sale online is rising in Cochabamba, El Alto and Santa Cruz; and Bolivian women and girls are exploited in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Panama and Peru. Tren de Aragua is reported to be involved in trafficking in Bolivia.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Bolivia

cases.n: Paraguay — 47,000 children in criadazgo domestic servitude (US TIP 2025)
cases.victims_note: estimate of children in criadazgo
cases.who: Families taking in children as unpaid domestic workers
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says criadazgo — compelling children to work as domestic workers — is a common form of trafficking in Paraguay; an estimated 47,000 children are in criadazgo, mostly girls (boys are 30 per cent), and many are highly vulnerable to sex and labour trafficking. Colombia's report describes the same practice.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Paraguay

cases.n: Haiti — restavek child domestic servitude and gang exploitation of children (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Observers report police and immigration officials complicit at the Haiti–Dominican Republic border.
cases.who: Host families (restavek); armed gangs
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says a large share of Haiti's trafficking cases involve children in restavek domestic servitude, often physically abused and unpaid, and that displacement from Port-au-Prince increased children's risk of sexual exploitation in the restavek system. Gangs exploit women and girls in sex trafficking; an international organization reported close to 50 per cent of gang members are children, with a 70 per cent rise in child recruitment in 2024.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Haiti

cases.n: Jamaica — child sex trafficking in resort towns; 6.3% of 12–17-year-olds (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Endemic corruption and official complicity, including within law enforcement, remained significant concerns.
cases.who: Family members, 'dons', foreign and local buyers
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report cites a 2023 prevalence study estimating 6.3 per cent of Jamaican children aged 12–17 had experienced conditions indicative of trafficking. Children are subjected to sex trafficking in resort areas frequented by tourists, sometimes with parental involvement, and men pay girls or their families for sex in some communities.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Jamaica

cases.n: Costa Rica — child sex trafficking on Pacific coast and borders (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Traffickers in coastal tourist zones
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers subject Costa Rican women and children to sex trafficking, especially in Pacific coastal zones and near the northern and southern borders, where social tolerance increases children's vulnerability; girls from Nicaragua, Panama, the Dominican Republic and Venezuela are also identified as victims.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Costa Rica

cases.n: Honduras, El Salvador, Guatemala — gangs exploit girls; North American offenders (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Gangs and criminal organizations; foreign offenders
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP reports say criminal organizations including gangs exploit girls in sex trafficking in urban Honduras and Guatemala, and that men from Canada and the US exploit Honduran children. In El Salvador, foreign tourists sexually exploit children and the rapid growth of tourism has created new risks; an estimated 140,000–200,000 Salvadoran children have a parent abroad or detained. Guatemalan children are exploited in Mexico and the US and in live-streamed abuse.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Honduras; El Salvador; Guatemala

cases.n: Europol: at least 10,000 unaccompanied migrant children missing in Europe (2016)
cases.victims_note: Europol called it likely conservative; 5,000 missing in Italy and 1,000 in Sweden
cases.who: Europol; organized crime exploiting the migrant flow
cases.d: On 31 January 2016 Europol's chief of staff Brian Donald told The Observer that at least 10,000 unaccompanied children had disappeared after arriving in Europe, 5,000 of them in Italy and 1,000 in Sweden, and that Europol had evidence some had been sexually exploited. He said an entire criminal infrastructure had developed over 18 months around exploiting the migrant flow, with many arrests in Germany and Hungary. Save the Children estimated 26,000 unaccompanied children arrived in 2015.
cases.cite: The Observer via Christian Science Monitor, 1 Feb 2016

cases.n: Romania–UK 'loverboy' network dismantled — 21 arrested (Eurojust, 2020)
cases.who: Romanian organized criminal group using the 'loverboy' method
cases.d: On 9 September 2020 a Romanian–UK Joint Investigation Team supported by Eurojust arrested 21 members of a hierarchical group active since 2009 that seduced vulnerable Romanian girls with false promises of relationships, exploited minors in prostitution in Romania until they turned 18, and then moved them to the UK, Ireland and Germany. Thirty-two house searches were carried out (23 in Romania, 9 in the UK). Eurojust said Romania and the UK had cooperated in 76 trafficking investigations in four years.
cases.cite: Eurojust press release, 18 Sep 2020

cases.n: Galați/Brăila — 'loverboy' ring exploiting minors in Western Europe (2021)
cases.who: Four suspects detained by DIICOT/BCCO
cases.d: In February 2021 Romanian organised-crime police and DIICOT prosecutors searched eight addresses in Galați and Brăila and detained four suspects for human trafficking, trafficking of minors and pimping. Investigators said that from August 2013 the group recruited girls and young women by the 'loverboy' method, hid minors in intermediate lodgings until they turned 18, then exploited them in Western Europe, earning about €350,000; nine victims, minor and adult, had been identified.
cases.cite: Știri pe Surse (via News.ro), 10 Feb 2021

cases.n: Romania — girls in state institutions at risk; victims sent across Europe (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Alleged complicity, misconduct and negligence by government employees in cases involving children in government-run homes remained a concern.
cases.who: Traffickers; staff of some government-run institutions
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says most identified victims are women and girls exploited in Romania and in Austria, France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK; children in government-run institutions, particularly girls in homes for persons with disabilities, are at risk of sex trafficking; and Roma children as young as 11 are 'sold' into marriage. Courts convicted 161 traffickers (143 for sex trafficking) and 600 victims were identified in 2024.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Romania

cases.n: Bulgaria — girls trafficked to Western Europe; exploitation in state institutions (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Corruption in law enforcement and the judiciary and impunity for complicit officials were pervasive; 34 convicted traffickers received suspended sentences.
cases.who: Traffickers; Roma forced marriages to third-country nationals
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Bulgarian women and girls in sex trafficking throughout Western Europe and in Sofia, resort areas and border towns, and cites a UN special rapporteur finding that child sexual exploitation, including potential sex trafficking, was prevalent among children in government-run institutions. Courts convicted 31 traffickers; only eight received custodial sentences.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Bulgaria

cases.n: Moldova — children recruited online; institution leavers at risk (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: A former police officer was convicted of labour trafficking (20 years); corruption and complicity remained significant concerns.
cases.who: Traffickers using social media and fake job ads
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers increasingly use social media and video chat to recruit children through fake job ads and exploit them in commercial sex, use abuse material as a grooming method, and target children in or leaving state institutions. Courts convicted 33 traffickers (22 for sex trafficking) in 2024.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Moldova

cases.n: Ukraine — wartime risk to evacuated institutional children; officials allegedly complicit (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Officials of several state-run residential institutions were allegedly complicit or negligent in trafficking of children in their care; no complicit officials convicted for the eighth year running.
cases.who: Criminal networks; some institution officials
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says child sex trafficking in Ukraine is underreported and criminals are trying to build online networks to exploit Ukrainian children internationally; children evacuated from at least 195 facilities, including those with disabilities, are at high risk; and Ukrainian refugee women and children are vulnerable in Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Bulgaria and the UK. Ukraine convicted 24 traffickers in 2024, only six with prison terms.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Ukraine; Germany; France

cases.n: Albania — children exploited in tourist season; first trafficking convictions since 2021 (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Traffickers; families
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says traffickers exploit Albanian women and children in sex trafficking and forced labour, especially in tourist season; Roma and Balkan-Egyptian children are forced to beg; and Albanian migrants in Western Europe, particularly the UK, are vulnerable to forced criminality. Courts convicted two sex traffickers and two labour traffickers, the first convictions since 2021. In the UK, Albanians were the second most common nationality referred as potential victims in 2024 (2,492), 95 per cent as adults.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Albania; Home Office NRM statistics 2024

cases.n: UK — 5,999 child potential victims referred to the National Referral Mechanism (2024)
cases.victims_note: child referrals in 2024 (31% of 19,125); 416 Vietnamese children; 1,845 county-lines referrals
cases.who: Home Office (NRM)
cases.d: Home Office statistics show 19,125 potential victims of modern slavery referred in 2024, 31 per cent (5,999) children; 78 per cent of child referrals were boys and criminal exploitation was the most common type (48 per cent). UK nationals were 23 per cent of all referrals, three-quarters of them children; Vietnamese nationals were 11 per cent, 416 of them children. In 2017 the Times reported more than 150 Vietnamese minors had gone missing from UK care since 2015.
cases.cite: Home Office, Modern Slavery NRM and DtN statistics, end of year summary 2024; Thomson Reuters Foundation via VnExpress, 13 Oct 2017

cases.n: France — 10,000–15,000 French teenagers in child sex trafficking (NGO estimate, US TIP 2025)
cases.victims_note: NGO estimate 10,000–15,000 French teenage victims; 3,000–4,000 unaccompanied Comorian children on Mayotte
cases.who: Small networks of young French men using romance schemes
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report cites NGO estimates that 10,000 to 15,000 French teenagers are victims of child sex trafficking, says authorities estimate more than half of all trafficking victims in France are French girls and young women exploited by small 'romance' networks, and that traffickers recruit girls in government-funded shelters. Criminal networks force children, mostly from Romania and North Africa, to commit crimes.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — France

cases.n: Germany, Spain, Italy, Greece — romance-method pimps, Nigerian networks, unaccompanied children (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: 'Loverboy' traffickers; Nigerian cult-linked groups; Eastern European recruiters
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP reports say young male traffickers in Germany and Spain coerce girls into sex trafficking through sham romantic relationships; highly organized groups sometimes linked to Nigerian cult organizations exploit Nigerian women and girls in Germany and Italy, in Italy through debt and 'voodoo' rituals; Eastern European girls are recruited online for child sex trafficking in Italy; and in Greece unaccompanied children are vulnerable to sex trafficking and Roma children from Albania, Bulgaria and Romania are forced to beg.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Germany; Spain; Italy; Greece

cases.n: Lebanon — Chez Maurice and Silver-B: about 75 Syrian women freed from sex-trafficking ring (2016)
cases.victims_note: about 75 Syrian women freed in March 2016; a 17-year-old Syrian girl found at the same premises in 2011
cases.cover: Chez Maurice was raided in late 2011 when a 17-year-old Syrian girl was found trapped there, closed for about three months and reopened. A survivor told Legal Agenda a trafficker claimed he had 'bought the state'.
cases.who: Chez Maurice and Silver-B brothels
cases.d: In March 2016 Lebanese security forces freed as many as 75 Syrian women from two brothels, Chez Maurice and Silver-B, in the Maameltein red-light district of Jounieh, and arrested and indicted over a dozen people on sex-trafficking charges. HRW said Syrian refugee women were at particular risk and that the same premises had been raided in 2011, when a 17-year-old Syrian girl was found, and later reopened. Lebanon's police identified 87 trafficking victims in 2016, mainly these survivors.
cases.cite: Human Rights Watch, 29 Jul 2016; Al Jazeera, 11 Feb 2020

cases.n: Jordan and Türkiye — Syrian refugee girls in forced marriages and sex trafficking (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: Türkiye: no investigations of complicit officials reported, though corruption and complicity remained significant concerns.
cases.who: Families and brokers arranging unofficial marriages
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says Syrian girls in Türkiye — which hosted about 2.9 million displaced Syrians — are forced into marriages in unofficial religious ceremonies, particularly in poor rural regions, and then subjected to domestic servitude and sex trafficking. In Jordan, Syrian refugee women and girls have been sold into forced marriages, and in 2022 authorities investigated a mother for allegedly exploiting her two daughters with foreign tourists.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Türkiye; Jordan

cases.n: Iraq — officials allegedly coerce ISIS-affiliated families, including children, into sex (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: An international organization reported in 2024 that officials coerce family members of detained children into sex acts in exchange for security clearances or civil documents; the government reported no action on official complicity.
cases.who: Security and military officials (alleged, per an international organization); criminal gangs
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says women and girls in IDP camps whose relatives have alleged ISIS ties may face sexual exploitation and sex trafficking by security and military officials, and that some officials allegedly exploit such families, including children, in exchange for documents. Criminal gangs reportedly exploit Syrian women and girls at pilgrimage sites, and Yezidi survivors remain at risk of re-trafficking.
cases.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Iraq

cases.n: US Angel Watch Center — 10,000+ notifications to foreign countries on travelling sex offenders
cases.who: US Homeland Security Investigations; CBP; US Marshals Service
cases.d: Under International Megan's Law (signed 2016), the Angel Watch Center notifies foreign governments when US registered child sex offenders plan to travel. DHS says that since 2016 it has made more than 10,000 notifications to foreign countries and notified the State Department of more than 3,500 passports carrying a sex-offender endorsement. HSI child-exploitation arrests rose to 3,771 in 2019 (ABC7, at the centre's ribbon-cutting).
cases.cite: DHS/HSI 'Angel Watch Center' page; WJLA/ABC7, 14 Nov 2019; Public Law 114-119

cases.n: UK — IICSA finds gaps let known offenders abuse children abroad (2020)
cases.cover: IICSA found travel restrictions were rarely used: 11 of 5,551 Sexual Harm Prevention Orders in 2017/18 and six Sexual Risk Orders in force in March 2019.
cases.who: UK Home Office, police, courts
cases.d: The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse report on the protection of children outside the UK (January 2020) found that only 11 of the 5,551 Sexual Harm Prevention Orders made in 2017/18 included foreign-travel restrictions, that 361 UK nationals sought consular help after arrest abroad for child sex offences in 2013–2017, and that there appear to have been only about eight successful UK prosecutions since 1997 for offences committed abroad, including Keith Morris (18.5 years, Kenya) and Mark Frost (Thailand).
cases.cite: IICSA, 'The Protection of Children Outside the United Kingdom', January 2020

cases.n: ECPAT 'Offenders on the Move' — Global Study on Sexual Exploitation of Children in Travel and Tourism (2016)
cases.who: ECPAT International and partners (High-Level Task Force chaired by Najat Maalla M'jid)
cases.d: Published 12 May 2016 after two years' work, the study found sexual exploitation of children in travel and tourism had grown despite 20 years of effort, as international arrivals rose from 527 million to 1.135 billion a year. It found there is no typical offender: most are domestic or regional travellers and 'situational' offenders rather than Western paedophiles; the internet has opened new pathways; and conviction rates are alarmingly low. It identified the US and Canada as source countries for offenders and Europe as a source, with exploitation rising in Central and Eastern Europe.
cases.cite: ECPAT International, Global Study on SECTT, 12 May 2016

cases.n: Peter Dalglish — former UN official jailed 9 years in Nepal for abusing two boys (2019)
cases.who: Peter John Dalglish (Canadian humanitarian, founder of Street Kids International)
cases.d: Nepal Police's Central Investigation Bureau arrested Dalglish, a Canadian who had worked for UN agencies including as a child-labour adviser in Nepal in 2002, at his home in Kavre on 7 April 2018, where boys aged 12 and 14 were found. On 8 July 2019 the Kavre District Court sentenced him to nine years and ordered compensation of Rs 500,000 to each boy. He denied the charges and said he would appeal. Al Jazeera reported fears that foreign offenders were using aid work or philanthropy as cover in Nepal.
cases.cite: Kathmandu Post, 8 Jul 2019; Al Jazeera, 9 Jul 2019

nets.n: Black Axe (Neo-Black Movement of Africa confraternity)
nets.reach_note: US TIP 2025 says cult-linked Nigerian groups traffic women and girls in Italy, Spain, the UK and Germany but does not name Black Axe; only Italian prosecutions were verified here.
nets.d: Nigerian confraternity whose members in Italy were arrested in 2016 for 'mafia conspiracy, drug trafficking, exploitation of prostitution and violent crimes'. A Palermo court convicted 14 in 2018; in 2019 another Palermo court rejected the mafia-association charge for five others.
nets.cite: Wikipedia 'Black Axe (confraternity)'; BlogSicilia 2018; Il Fatto Quotidiano 2019

nets.reach_note: US TIP 2025 reports Tren de Aragua trafficking in Colombia, Peru and Bolivia, and transfers from Cúcuta to Argentina, Ecuador and Peru; operations in Ecuador/Argentina are stated only as destinations.
nets.d: Transnational criminal organization originating in Venezuela. US TIP 2025 says it operates sex-trafficking networks in Colombia, using daily-debt lodging (pagadiarios) to control victims, and has affiliated groups in Peru.
nets.cite: US TIP Report 2025 — Colombia, Peru, Bolivia

flows.n: Edo State → Libya → Italy (sex trafficking of women and girls)
flows.size_note: Nigerian female sea arrivals in Italy in 2016 (IOM data); at least four in five forced into prostitution
flows.d: Women and girls, most from Edo State, are moved overland through Niger and Libya and by boat to Italy, bound by debt and oaths. IOM recorded an almost 600 per cent rise in potential victims arriving by sea in 2014–2017.
flows.cite: IOM via UN News, Jul 2017; Thomson Reuters Foundation, Sep 2018

flows.n: Nigeria → gold-mining regions of Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire
flows.d: Organized networks transport Nigerian women and girls to mining regions in Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire for sex trafficking; in Kédougou victims include girls as young as 12.

flows.n: United States → Cambodia (travelling child sex offenders)
flows.size_note: three men returned under Operation Twisted Traveler in Aug 2009; Boyajian made 35 trips to Asia in nine years
flows.d: US men, several already convicted at home, travelled repeatedly to Cambodia to buy children; prosecuted in Los Angeles under the PROTECT Act.

flows.n: Vietnam → Svay Pak, Cambodia (girls sold to brothels)
flows.d: Most children in Svay Pak brothels were ethnic Vietnamese, many sold by destitute families; US TIP 2025 still reports ethnic Vietnamese women and girls exploited in Cambodian cities and tourist areas.

flows.n: Karamoja, Uganda → Nairobi (girls for domestic servitude and sex)
flows.d: Cross-border rings ferry women and underage girls from Karamoja to Nairobi for domestic servitude or sex trafficking.

flows.n: Ethiopia → Saudi Arabia (children in forced begging rings)
flows.d: Organized begging rings exploit Ethiopian women and children in Saudi Arabia.

flows.n: Ethiopia → Djibouti (girls in domestic servitude and sex trafficking)
flows.d: Ethiopian girls are exploited in domestic servitude and sex trafficking in Djibouti and Sudan.

flows.n: United Kingdom → The Gambia (travelling offenders)
flows.d: European tourists, primarily from the UK, reportedly travel to The Gambia to exploit children; networks use European and Gambian travel agencies.

flows.n: Italy / Germany / Switzerland → Kenya coast (tourist offenders)
flows.d: The 2006 UNICEF–Government study found Italian, German and Swiss tourists made up 44 per cent of clients of exploited children on the coast; Kenyans were 38 per cent.

flows.n: France → Madagascar (tourist offenders)
flows.d: Foreign tourists, often from France, exploit Malagasy children.

flows.n: Europe → Tangier, Morocco (tourist offenders in vacation rentals)
flows.d: NGOs report tourists exploit children in Tangier in vacation rentals owned and managed by European nationals.

flows.n: Dzaleka camp, Malawi → South Africa ('Southern Route')
flows.d: The camp is a waypoint for criminal networks moving migrants south, some of whom end up in sex trafficking or forced labour, particularly in South Africa.

flows.n: Nepal → India (girls and women to brothels)
flows.size_note: lower bound of published annual estimates (5,000–10,000 per year); not an official count
flows.d: Recruitment by false job, marriage and online romance offers across the open border to brothels in Kolkata, Mumbai and elsewhere.
flows.cite: US TIP 2025 — Nepal; Wikipedia 'Human trafficking in Nepal'

flows.n: Nepal → Kamathipura, Mumbai
flows.d: Large numbers of Nepalese women and girls trafficked into Kamathipura in recent decades.

flows.n: Bangladesh → India (women and girls)
flows.d: Bangladeshi women and girls exploited in sex trafficking in India; children estimated at 40% of Bangladeshi sex-trafficking victims abroad.

flows.n: Pakistan → China ('bride' trafficking)
flows.size_note: girls and women on FIA list, 2018–June 2019
flows.d: Brokers sold poor Pakistani girls and women, many Christian, to Chinese men as brides.

flows.n: Kachin State, Myanmar → Yunnan and beyond, China ('bride' trafficking)
flows.size_note: cases reported by Myanmar government in 2017; HRW says real number likely much higher
flows.d: Women and girls sold for $3,000–13,000 to Chinese families.

flows.n: Northern Vietnam → China (forced marriage)
flows.d: Hmong and other ethnic-minority women and girls lured or abducted to China for forced marriage.

flows.n: Laos → China (forced marriage, surrogacy)
flows.d: Lao women and girls kidnapped or recruited via marriage brokers to China.

flows.n: Singapore → Batam / Riau Islands (travelling offenders)
flows.d: Extraterritorial child sexual exploitation is prevalent in the Riau Islands bordering Singapore.

flows.n: Middle East → Puncak, West Java ('contract marriages')
flows.d: Middle Eastern tourists pay for short 'contract marriages' with girls as young as nine.

flows.n: Australia / UK / US / Japan / NZ → Philippines (foreign offenders)
flows.d: Most foreign offenders in the Philippines are from Australia, Japan, New Zealand, the UK and the US, many already convicted or charged at home.

flows.n: Europe → Pattaya, Thailand (travelling offenders)
flows.d: Repeat offenders from Switzerland and the UK, previously convicted at home, abused boys in Pattaya and elsewhere; the Swiss bar also served European clients.

flows.n: Burma / Cambodia / Laos → Thailand (children in sex trafficking)
flows.d: Children from Thailand, Burma, Cambodia and Laos increasingly sex-trafficked in brothels, massage parlours, bars and hotels; many Lao women and girls exploited in Thailand.

flows.n: Venezuela → Colombia (displaced girls and women)
flows.d: Displaced Venezuelan women and girls exploited in sex trafficking and webcam studios; Tren de Aragua moves victims through Cúcuta.

flows.n: Venezuela → Trinidad and Tobago (women and girls)
flows.d: Sex-trafficking victims are mainly women and girls from Venezuela, Colombia, the Dominican Republic and Guyana; NGOs allege officials facilitate transport and entry.

flows.n: Cúcuta → Ecuador, Peru, Argentina (Tren de Aragua transfers)
flows.d: Tren de Aragua reportedly used Cúcuta's transport hub to move trafficking victims to Argentina, Ecuador and Peru.

flows.n: United States → Medellín (travelling offenders)
flows.size_note: US convictions linked to the Medellín offensive by May 2026
flows.d: US men travelled repeatedly to Medellín (one 48 times in two years) to exploit girls; prosecuted in Miami.

flows.n: Cartagena → Panama, Mexico, Miami, Bahamas ('La Madame' network)
flows.d: Young women sent individually abroad, coached to avoid airport scrutiny.

flows.n: United States → Puerto Plata / Sosúa (travelling offenders)
flows.d: US men prosecuted under the PROTECT Act for abusing boys and girls on the north coast; joint HSI–Dominican operations in tourist towns.

flows.n: Guatemala / Honduras → Mexico → United States (children in sex trafficking)
flows.d: Guatemalan and Honduran adults and children exploited in sex trafficking in Mexico, the US, Belize and El Salvador.

flows.n: Bolivia → Argentina / Brazil (women and girls)
flows.d: Bolivian women and girls exploited in sex trafficking in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Panama and Peru.

flows.n: US / Europe → Cusco and the Peruvian Amazon (tourist offenders)
flows.d: Tourists from the US and Europe exploit children in Cusco, Lima and the Amazon; boats take tourists to remote river venues.

flows.n: Romania → UK / Ireland / Germany ('loverboy' recruitment)
flows.d: Girls groomed as minors in Romania, then moved at 18 to the UK, Ireland and Germany for sexual exploitation.

flows.n: Romania → Western Europe (sex trafficking of women and girls)
flows.d: Most identified Romanian victims are women and girls exploited in Austria, France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK.

flows.n: Vietnam → United Kingdom (children for cannabis farms, nail bars)
flows.size_note: Vietnamese children referred to the UK NRM in 2024
flows.d: Vietnamese children and adults exploited in cannabis cultivation, nail salons and forced criminality; many children went missing from local-authority care.
flows.cite: Home Office NRM 2024; US TIP 2025 — UK

flows.n: Syria → Lebanon (refugee women and girls into sex trafficking)
flows.d: Criminal groups recruit Syrian women and girls with false job offers and exploit them in Lebanese brothels; Syrian children held in bonded labour in the Beqaa.

flows.n: United Kingdom → Kenya (Keith Morris)
flows.d: Keith Morris was jailed for 18.5 years in the UK for 10 sexual offences against vulnerable children in Kenya, one of about eight UK prosecutions for offences abroad since 1997.

flows.n: United Kingdom → Thailand (Mark Frost)
flows.d: Former teacher and scout leader abused boys in Thailand and streamed abuse to another European man.

flows.n: Canada → Nepal (aid-worker offender)
flows.d: A Canadian humanitarian working with street children abused boys at his home in Nepal.

- Children were 38 per cent of all detected victims in 2022; detected child victims rose 31 per cent vs 2019, girls up 38 per cent. Women and girls were 61 per cent of detected victims; 60 per cent of girl victims were trafficked for sexual exploitation; 45 per cent of boys for forced labour and 47 per cent for other purposes (forced criminality, begging). Total detected victims +25 per cent vs 2019.
- Regional child shares (GLOTIP 2024, read from the PDF): Central America and the Caribbean, Sub-Saharan Africa and North Africa recorded the highest shares of children, around 60 per cent of detected victims, followed by East Asia and the Pacific and South Asia (p.45). Sub-Saharan Africa: children 61 per cent of detected victims in 2022, girls 42 per cent (p.122). Central America and the Caribbean: girls 52 per cent of detected victims, over 80 per cent female (p.128). North Africa: boys 33 per cent (largest group); GCC countries: children only about 3 per cent (p.114). South Asia: boys about a quarter, girls 17 per cent (p.152). East Asia and the Pacific: boys 7 per cent; females about 80 per cent (p.146). Europe and North America detect more adults than children. Exact child share for South America and Western/Southern Europe not extracted (PDF text encoding garbled some figures) — read the figures in the PDF directly before publishing those.
- African victims account for 31 per cent of detected cross-border flows; nationals of African conflict countries made up about 2,000 victims detected in Europe.
